statement: A farm collects $200$ eggs and packs them into cartons that each hold $12$ eggs, filling one carton completely before starting the next. How many more eggs are needed to fill the last, partly filled carton?

choices.misconception: I divided on a calculator, $200 \div 12 = 16.67$, and read the $6$ after the decimal point as the $6$ eggs still needed.
I found $200 = 12 \cdot 16 + 8$ and gave the remainder $8$, which is how many eggs are already in the last carton, not how many are missing.
I gave the quotient of $200 \div 12$, which is the number of full cartons, $16$.
I counted all the cartons that get used, $16$ full ones plus the partly filled one, and answered $17$.

hints: Find how many cartons can be filled completely and how many eggs are left over.
Divide $200$ by $12$ and look at the remainder. The last carton holds that many eggs.
$200 = 12 \cdot 16 + 8$, so the last carton has $8$ eggs. It holds $12$.

solutions.reliable: Since $12 \cdot 16 = 192$ and $200 - 192 = 8$, the farm fills $16$ cartons and has $8$ eggs in a seventeenth carton. That carton needs $12 - 8 = 4$ more eggs.
solutions.elegant: The next multiple of $12$ after $200$ is $12 \cdot 17 = 204$, so $204 - 200 = 4$ more eggs are needed.
